root_cause.text: `cgwb_release_workfn()` in `mm/backing-dev.c` dropped the last reference to `wb->blkcg_css` with `css_put()` before calling `blkcg_unpin_online()`, allowing the `blkcg`/`css` object to be freed and then dereferenced, causing a use-after-free in the blk-cgroup writeback release path.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE text says `cgwb_release_workfn() calls css_put(wb->blkcg_css) and then later accesses wb->blkcg_css again via blkcg_unpin_online()`, and the patch fixes it by moving `blkcg_unpin_online(wb->blkcg_css)` before `css_put(wb->blkcg_css)`; the reported KASAN splat shows the UAF occurs in `blkcg_unpin_online` after `css_free_rwork_fn -> blkcg_css_free -> kfree` freed the object.

intent_record.intent_summary: Reorder blkcg css release in cgwb teardown so online unpinning happens before dropping the css reference.
intent_record.what: In `cgwb_release_workfn()`, the `css_put(wb->blkcg_css);` call and the `mutex_unlock(&wb->bdi->cgwb_release_mutex);` call were moved to occur after `blkcg_unpin_online(wb->blkcg_css);` instead of before it.
intent_record.how: This changes the release sequence so the blkcg css remains held while `blkcg_unpin_online()` runs, ensuring the blkcg object is still valid when the online pin is dropped and that any resulting destruction is triggered only after the unpin operation completes.

candidates.rationale: This drops the last reference to wb->blkcg_css before blkcg_unpin_online() runs, which can free the blkcg/css object and leave the later unpinning dereferencing freed memory.
